paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD is worth singing about, and He is worth telling EVERYBODY about. The writer says to sing a new song, to proclaim His salvation day after day, and to declare His glory among the nations (Psalm 96:1-3). That's not a once-a-week thing, and it's not a whisper. The reason is simple: "great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised" (Psalm 96:4).

Why does it matter to you? Because the writer says all the gods of the nations are idols, but it is the LORD who made the heavens (Psalm 96:5). Nothing else deserves your whole heart the way He does. And you don't stand outside waiting, because the writer says to bring an offering and enter His courts (Psalm 96:8). Then comes the news worth passing along: "The LORD reigns!" (Psalm 96:10). The world is firmly established, and He will judge the peoples with equity.

Then the writer lets the whole creation join in: heavens, earth, sea, fields, and trees (Psalm 96:11-12). They sing for joy because "He is coming—He is coming to judge the earth" (Psalm 96:13). He will judge in righteousness and in His faithfulness, so His coming is good news worth singing about. That's why my ovens stay ready, friend, and why yours should too. Go sing, go tell somebody, and let your song be LOUDER than mine, which is not hard!
